chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted his father, on the authority of Muhammad ibn authority of Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khazzaz, on the authority of Talha ibn Zayd, on the authority of Ja'far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his forefathers, on the authority of Ali (peace be upon them) that God's Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Four [characteristics] are from the traditions of the Messengers: perfumes, women, using the siwak, and henna.

key_terms.سُنَنِ: traditions or practices of the prophets

ai.seo_question: What are the four traditions of the Prophets mentioned in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith in *Al-Khisal* to highlight that these four practices—perfume, marriage, dental hygiene via siwak, and henna—are not merely cultural habits but established *sunnah* shared by all divine Messengers. This classification elevates them to acts of worship and natural disposition (*fitrah*), emphasizing their role in maintaining physical purity, social stability, and aesthetic beauty as prescribed by God. The inclusion of 'women' specifically points to the institution of marriage, underscoring the Prophetic model of family life as a core component of religious tradition.
